name: Sapir Organization

summary.text: The Sapir Organization is a New York real-estate company founded by Tamir Sapir (1947–2014), a Georgian-born investor, and run from 2006 by his son Alex Sapir as chairman and president. It owned 11 Madison Avenue and, with the Bayrock Group, co-developed the Trump SoHo hotel-condominium through the sponsor entity Bayrock/Sapir Organization LLC. Fifteen buyers sued the sponsor, Donald Trump, Alex Sapir and Tevfik Arif in 2010 alleging inflated sales figures; the suit was settled in November 2011 with 90 percent refunds of deposits and no admission of wrongdoing.

facts.claim: Tamir Sapir, founder of the Sapir Organization, died in September 2014; he had emigrated from Tbilisi in 1973 and founded Zar Realty Management in 1993, buying distressed assets and upgrading them into commercial properties.
facts.quote: He founded Zar Realty Management in 1993, buying distressed assets and upgrading them into commercial properties

facts.claim: In 2006 Tamir Sapir named Alex Sapir chairman and president of the Sapir Organization; a 2008 profile said the company owned 11 Madison Avenue, then the U.S. headquarters of Credit Suisse.
facts.quote: In 2006, Tamir Sapir named Alex the chairman and president of the Sapir Organization

sources.title: Profile: Tamir Sapir and the Sapir Organization

facts.claim: To build Trump SoHo, Bayrock teamed up with Alex Sapir; the Sapir Organization and Bayrock Group invested $450 million in the project, which carried the Trump name under licence.
facts.quote: To build the Trump SoHo, Bayrock would team up with Alex Sapir, the son of billionaire Tamir Sapir

facts.claim: In August 2010 fifteen buyers sued in Manhattan federal court, naming the sponsor Bayrock/Sapir Organization LLC, Donald J. Trump, Alex Sapir and Tevfik Arif, alleging they had been told as many as 60 percent of units were sold when only 16 percent of the hotel-condo units at 246 Spring Street had been sold.
facts.quote: The defendants included the Bayrock/Sapir Organization LLC, which is the project's sponsor; Donald J. Trump; Alex Sapir; and Tevfik Arif

sources.title: Donald Trump sued for fraud over condo

facts.claim: In November 2011 the buyers' federal suit was settled, with the buyers receiving 90 percent of the $5.197 million in deposits they had put down; the defence said there was no admission of guilt by the developers.
facts.quote: they will get 90 percent of the $5.197 million in deposits they combined to have put down on $16.914 million worth of apartments

facts.claim: A Manhattan district attorney's investigation into the alleged sales-figure fraud was closed; as part of the settlement the buyers notified prosecutors that they no longer wished to assist the investigation.
facts.quote: As part of the lawsuit settlement, the buyers had to notify prosecutors that they no longer wished to help the investigation.

openQuestions: The entity is in the seed list only. Wikipedia's entry on the building gives 2015 for a settlement with the same 90 percent figure, conflicting with the November 2011 reporting; the 2011 settlement is recorded.
The $450 million investment figure comes from a feature account (Worldcrunch/WGBH) and was not confirmed in a filing.
The site's Sater dossier refers to 'a SoHo tower'; Sater's own role in the Sapir partnership was not researched here.
